name: Mohammed Arkoun
shortBio: Algerian-French philosopher of Islam who pioneered Applied Islamology, deploying historical epistemology and discourse analysis to distinguish the open Qur’anic event from closed orthodoxies of "Islamic Reason."
centralQuestion: What becomes thinkable in Islamic philosophy when we examine the "unthought" and "unthinkable" boundaries constructed by medieval orthodoxies?

keyWorks.title: Pour une critique de la raison islamique (Critique of Islamic Reason)
keyWorks.description: Applies historical-critical epistemology and Foucault’s archaeology to excavate classical Arabic humanism and marginalized heterodoxy.

keyWorks.title: The Unthought in Contemporary Islamic Thought
keyWorks.description: Programmatic manifesto for Applied Islamology bridging critical theory, hermeneutics, and Mediterranean intellectual history.
